name: Lensmor
summary: Trade-show prospecting for B2B teams: search events for free, then spend credits to open exhibitor, attendee and visitor lists and to reveal verified emails and phone numbers, with an AI agent that shortlists shows that fit your ideal customer profile.
best_for: B2B sales and marketing teams that exhibit at or prospect around trade shows and want exhibitor and attendee lists per event, with verified contacts revealed only for the accounts that fit
skip_if: you need a general B2B contact database rather than event data, or a budget of $499 a month is out of reach for your team
honest_knock: The entry price is high: $499 a month for Basic, and the free start is a one-time grant of 2,000 credits, not a free plan. Credits go fast: one full event unlock is 5,000 credits, and every phone number another 150. Visitor data depends on the event and needs a paid plan. Subscription fees are non-refundable except where the law requires otherwise, and the subscription renews unless you cancel before the end of the billing cycle.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic · flat price for a workspace of up to 5 seats with 35,000 credits a month
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-26 on lensmor.com/pricing and Lensmor's billing policy in its help centre; dollar amounts, the pages do not name the currency) Lensmor sells credits. Every new account starts with 2,000 free credits, without a credit card. Basic is $499 a month or $4,990 a year, for 35,000 credits a month and a shared workspace of up to 5 seats; the credits reset every month, also on annual billing. Growth is $14,900 a year for 1,500,000 credits per annual term and up to 10 seats, with priority email and WhatsApp support. Enterprise is a custom annual agreement with API access and integrations. Active paid subscribers can buy add-on credits: 10,000 for $249, 25,000 for $549 or 60,000 for $1,199, valid for 12 months. What credits buy: unlocking an event's exhibitors and public-signal attendees costs 2,000 credits, full access including visitors 5,000 (or 3,000 to add visitors later), a returned email 15, a returned phone number 150, and a search by exhibitor 50 when it finds matches. Unused subscription credits do not roll over, and subscription fees are non-refundable.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Lensmor on the 2,000 free credits of an account we created. The event from the test plan was not in Lensmor, so the test used Web Summit Lisbon 2026: the list of 310 exhibitors stood after about 7 minutes and a list of 105 IBM people after about 11. Opening the base data of that one event used all 2,000 free credits at once, with no question to confirm, so revealing a single e-mail address (15 credits) was already short of credits. Opening an event in full costs 5,000 credits. The card page of Basic asked $499.00 due today with no trial and was closed with nothing filled in. Account and start: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. The test itself ran on 19 November 2026 from about 09:25 to 09:37 and was written up by the first test agent; the screenshots were made later the same day in the same signed-in session, so the times and some steps come from that report and were not seen again. The onboarding had a company website filled in already and analysed it (Industry: Information Technology); the role chosen was Exhibitor. Then the app said 2,000 free Credits have been added to your account, and at about 09:27 the 2,000 credits were visible. No card was asked. The interface was in English. The dossier name is Lensmor and the review is on MSS (mss/lensmor-review.html). Core action, an exhibitor list and a people list for one trade show: the event in the test plan could not be found, so a large public trade show was chosen, Web Summit Lisbon 2026 (Nov 9-12, 2026, Lisbon, MEO Arena & FIL, 50,000 - 100,000 expected attendees, tabs Exhibitors (310) and Attendees (43,260), data updated Nov 16, 2026). At about 09:32 the first usable list stood: 310 exhibitors, of which 8 were visible before the event was opened, with match scores such as 96/100 and High Fit labels; about 7 minutes from the start. Opening the base data of the event cost 2,000 credits and took the balance from 2,000 to 0, with no question to confirm. At about 09:36 the first people list stood, 105 IBM contacts, about 11 minutes from the start. Without a filter the Attendees tab gave 3,317 results with source Exhibitor, and a banner said the list currently shows mostly people from exhibiting companies, with an upgrade offer for 39,943 event visitors. The columns are Email (Reveal Email), LinkedIn, Telephone (Reveal Phone), LinkedIn Activity and Outreach. Reveal Email for one person opened Reveal Contact Information: Price per email 15 Credits, Total cost 15 Credits, Current balance 0 Credits, Credits short 15 Credits, with Cancel and Get more Credits; Cancel was pressed and nothing was spent. Before the event was opened the Export button was off and most exhibitors were Locked. Time: about 7 minutes to the first exhibitor list and about 11 minutes to a usable people list (clock times estimated by the test agent). Plans: On the public pricing page lensmor.com/pricing: Basic $499 / month, billed monthly, with a Monthly or Yearly switch, 35,000 credits per month, about 7 complete events per month, a shared workspace for up to 5 seats and credits that reset monthly; the yearly price of Basic in the app was $4,990 (2 months free, $5,988 struck through). Growth (Most popular) $14,900 / year, billed annually, 1,500,000 credits per annual term, about 300 complete events per year, up to 10 seats, credits that reset at the annual renewal. Enterprise Custom, annual agreement, Contact Sales. The page says you start with 2,000 free credits and that no credit card is required. Credit costs seen in the app: opening the base data of one event cost 2,000 credits, opening an event in full costs 5,000 credits (2,000 base plus 3,000 visitor data), a revealed e-mail address costs 15 credits per person, and the pricing page gives 150 credits per phone number. Checkout: Choose Basic in the app opened the payment page of Lensmor (Clink) at once, with Due Today $499.00, no trial, and fields for the card, the card holder and the billing address. Nothing was filled in and nothing was paid. This step comes from the report of the first test agent; no image of it was kept. Cancelling: no plan was bought, so there was nothing to cancel, and the cancelling route was not tested. Not tested: Export (CSV or Excel, Google Sheets and HubSpot were seen in the menu and not clicked), mailing anyone, putting anyone in a sequence, Reveal Phone, LinkedIn Activity, Outreach messages, links with other tools and a paid plan. The event in the test plan could not be found; the test ran on Web Summit Lisbon 2026. Clean up: the account and the opened Web Summit data stay, with 0 credits. The own tab was closed and our onboarding tab was not touched. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Opening the base data of one event took all 2,000 free credits in one go, with no question to confirm, so the free start covers the base data of one event and nothing more: revealing one e-mail address afterwards was 15 credits short. A full event costs 5,000 credits, more than the free grant. Basic has no trial at the card page and asks $499.00 due today. The people list shows mostly staff of exhibiting companies; the visitors sit behind an upgrade.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Lensmor on the 2,000 free credits of an account we created. The event from the test plan was not in Lensmor, so the test used Web Summit Lisbon 2026: the list of 310 exhibitors stood after about 7 minutes and a list of 105 IBM people after about 11. Opening the base data of that one event used all 2,000 free credits at once, with no question to confirm, so revealing a single e-mail address (15 credits) was already short of credits. Opening an event in full costs 5,000 credits. The card page of Basic asked $499.00 due today with no trial and was closed with nothing filled in. Account and start: we created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. The test itself ran on 19 November 2026 from about 09:25 to 09:37 and was written up by the first test agent; the screenshots were made later the same day in the same signed-in session, so the times and some steps come from that report and were not seen again. The onboarding had a company website filled in already and analysed it (Industry: Information Technology); the role chosen was Exhibitor. Then the app said 2,000 free Credits have been added to your account, and at about 09:27 the 2,000 credits were visible. No card was asked. The interface was in English. The dossier name is Lensmor and the review is on MSS (mss/lensmor-review.html). Core action, an exhibitor list and a people list for one trade show: the event in the test plan could not be found, so a large public trade show was chosen, Web Summit Lisbon 2026 (Nov 9-12, 2026, Lisbon, MEO Arena & FIL, 50,000 - 100,000 expected attendees, tabs Exhibitors (310) and Attendees (43,260), data updated Nov 16, 2026). At about 09:32 the first usable list stood: 310 exhibitors, of which 8 were visible before the event was opened, with match scores such as 96/100 and High Fit labels; about 7 minutes from the start. Opening the base data of the event cost 2,000 credits and took the balance from 2,000 to 0, with no question to confirm. At about 09:36 the first people list stood, 105 IBM contacts, about 11 minutes from the start. Without a filter the Attendees tab gave 3,317 results with source Exhibitor, and a banner said the list currently shows mostly people from exhibiting companies, with an upgrade offer for 39,943 event visitors. The columns are Email (Reveal Email), LinkedIn, Telephone (Reveal Phone), LinkedIn Activity and Outreach. Reveal Email for one person opened Reveal Contact Information: Price per email 15 Credits, Total cost 15 Credits, Current balance 0 Credits, Credits short 15 Credits, with Cancel and Get more Credits; Cancel was pressed and nothing was spent. Before the event was opened the Export button was off and most exhibitors were Locked. Time: about 7 minutes to the first exhibitor list and about 11 minutes to a usable people list (clock times estimated by the test agent). Plans: On the public pricing page lensmor.com/pricing: Basic $499 / month, billed monthly, with a Monthly or Yearly switch, 35,000 credits per month, about 7 complete events per month, a shared workspace for up to 5 seats and credits that reset monthly; the yearly price of Basic in the app was $4,990 (2 months free, $5,988 struck through). Growth (Most popular) $14,900 / year, billed annually, 1,500,000 credits per annual term, about 300 complete events per year, up to 10 seats, credits that reset at the annual renewal. Enterprise Custom, annual agreement, Contact Sales. The page says you start with 2,000 free credits and that no credit card is required. Credit costs seen in the app: opening the base data of one event cost 2,000 credits, opening an event in full costs 5,000 credits (2,000 base plus 3,000 visitor data), a revealed e-mail address costs 15 credits per person, and the pricing page gives 150 credits per phone number. Checkout: Choose Basic in the app opened the payment page of Lensmor (Clink) at once, with Due Today $499.00, no trial, and fields for the card, the card holder and the billing address. Nothing was filled in and nothing was paid. This step comes from the report of the first test agent; no image of it was kept. Cancelling: no plan was bought, so there was nothing to cancel, and the cancelling route was not tested. Not tested: Export (CSV or Excel, Google Sheets and HubSpot were seen in the menu and not clicked), mailing anyone, putting anyone in a sequence, Reveal Phone, LinkedIn Activity, Outreach messages, links with other tools and a paid plan. The event in the test plan could not be found; the test ran on Web Summit Lisbon 2026. Clean up: the account and the opened Web Summit data stay, with 0 credits. The own tab was closed and our onboarding tab was not touched. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: Opening the base data of one event took all 2,000 free credits in one go, with no question to confirm, so the free start covers the base data of one event and nothing more: revealing one e-mail address afterwards was 15 credits short. A full event costs 5,000 credits, more than the free grant. Basic has no trial at the card page and asks $499.00 due today. The people list shows mostly staff of exhibiting companies; the visitors sit behind an upgrade.
